edition.notes: Volumes I and II of Lenker's series 'The Precious and Sacred Writings of Martin Luther', based on the Kaiser chronological edition with reference to the Erlangen and Walch editions. This translation covers only the opening of the lectures: volume I, 'Luther on the Creation', runs Genesis 1 to 4, and volume II, 'Luther on Sin and the Flood', runs Genesis 4 to 9. Luther lectured through Genesis 50, so this edition is a bounded part of the work and must not be read as the whole; the remainder reaches English only in the twentieth-century American Edition (Luther's Works 1 to 8, Concordia 1958 to 1966), which is in copyright. Lenker died in 1929 and the printing is of 1904, so this translation is in the public domain in the United States by date of publication.
edition.publication: Minneapolis: Lutherans in All Lands Co., 1904
edition.title: Commentary on Genesis, translated by John Nicholas Lenker

passages.context: Luther's exposition of Genesis 1 as Lenker prints it, the whole of the printed chapter, 291 paragraphs, from volume I of the translation. The printed lemmata run from "V. 2a. And the earth was waste and void" to "V. 30. And every green herb". The untitled introduction that opens the chapter argues about the age of the world and the order of the six days, but it prints no lemma at 1:1 and the extent is not widened to reach it; nor is there a lemma at 1:31.

work.author: Martin Luther
work.description: Luther's lectures on Genesis, delivered at Wittenberg between 1535 and 1545 and the last and longest of his exegetical courses, running the whole book from the creation to the death of Joseph. They were taken down by hearers, edited by Veit Dietrich and others, and first printed 1544 to 1554; the extent of the editors' hand in the printed text is disputed and the dispute belongs to this record rather than to any translation of it. The work is named here by its Latin title because the lectures were delivered and printed in Latin, and reaches the reader in English only in parts.
work.title: Enarrationes in Genesin
